request: Add a helper in accounts/views.py that checks if the post-login `next` URL is safe, and use it in the login view.

summary.result_text:
I added `_allow_redirect(redirect_url)` to `hc/accounts/views.py`, right after `POST_LOGIN_ROUTES`. I haven't run the code or any tests. My syntax check was blocked by a permission prompt.

The file is `hc/accounts/views.py`, not `accounts/views.py`. The login view and three other places already called `_allow_redirect`, but nothing defined it, so those calls would have raised `NameError`. The login view didn't need any edits.

The helper returns `True` only when all of these hold:
- **Present:** the value is a non-empty string.
- **Relative:** it has no scheme or host, so `https://evil.com` is rejected.
- **Local path:** it starts with `/` but not `//`, so scheme-relative `//evil.com` is rejected.
- **No tricks:** it contains no backslashes or control characters, since browsers can turn `/\evil.com` into `//evil.com`.
- **Allowed route:** the path resolves to a route listed in `POST_LOGIN_ROUTES`.

The existing callers are `_redirect_after_login`, `_check_2fa`, the magic-link branch of `login`, and `login_webauthn`.

I'd run the accounts tests (`./manage.py test hc.accounts`) to confirm.
